part2.question: A time when you organised a happy event successfully

segments.v: I want to talk about a surprise party for my grandmother's 70th birthday. It was last spring. My grandmother doesn't like big parties, so we made it a surprise. I prepared for two months. I called my relatives and made a group chat. My cousin decorated the restaurant and my uncle cooked the food. I made a slideshow with old family photos and music. On the day, we told my grandmother it was a normal lunch. When she came in, everyone shouted “Happy birthday”. She was very surprised and she cried. Everyone was very happy. I think the event was successful because my grandmother didn't know about it before and she was very happy.

part3.question: Do you prefer to prepare and organise an activity or just take part in an activity?

segments.v: I prefer to take part because organising is very tiring and stressful.
It depends on the event. For small, personal things, like my grandma's party, I really enjoy organising; there's a special
in seeing a plan come together. But for big events, I'd rather just take part. Organising means you spend the whole time
checking that everything is running smoothly, so you can't really relax and enjoy it. So I'd say I like organising when it's
when I want to have fun.

fluency.band9: It depends → organising small events (satisfaction) → taking part in big ones (why) → summary.

grammar.band9: “I'd rather + verb”, and “there's a special satisfaction in seeing…”.

analysis.keyDifference: Band 9 avoids a one-sided answer and explains the trade-off with a personal example.
